quests.title: First Blood
quests.description:
Easy. Sit up slowly - you've had a fall and the ground will still be there in a moment.

I'm Nakhtar. Farseer, for whatever that's worth out here, which on most days is a tent and an opinion.

I'm not going to ask you where you came from. You wouldn't have a good answer and I've stopped finding the bad ones interesting - you're the fourth this season and every one of you wakes up with sand in your mouth and the same look.

Here is the only question that matters today: can you still hold a weapon?

The valley's thick with mottled boars. Stupid, aggressive, and exactly the right size of problem for somebody who doesn't yet know what his own arms do.

Go and find out. Not for the valley's sake. For yours.
quests.accept_text: Out on the flat, anywhere west. The boars will find you before you find them.
quests.turn_in_text:
Still standing, and you came back by the road instead of across the rocks. Good - that's two things learned and you'll only remember one of them.

Sit down. Eat something. The valley's got more to say to you and it's in no hurry.

quests.title: Scorpid Trouble
quests.description:
The scorpids have been pushing further from the nest than they should. Three days running now.

I don't like things that change their habits for no reason. A boar is a boar every day of its life - that's what makes it useful for teaching. A scorpid that's started behaving differently is telling you something about the valley, and I'd rather read it early.

Could be nothing. Could be the same wrongness that's been creeping in here since before you arrived, which I'll talk to you about when I've got more than a feeling.

Thin the workers out. And watch their tails, not their claws - the claws are what they show you.

This is the last easy lesson I've got. Take it slowly.
quests.accept_text:
Out at the nest, on the flat. Thin the workers - there's no chasing needed in this one.

And watch their tails, not their claws. That's where the lesson is.
quests.turn_in_text: That'll keep them honest a while. You watched the tails, like I said - good, you listen. That's rarer than it should be. Now. You've done real work for this valley, twice now, and I don't say that lightly. Take something for it - pick whatever suits how you fight. You've earned the choice, not just the reward.

quests.title: Into the Den
quests.description:
Nakhtar talks. That's his function and I don't begrudge it, but you'll learn more in an hour underground than in a week of being told about it.

Kuraw. The Den's the shallow cave west of camp. Nothing in there should kill a careful person, which is exactly why I want you in THAT one first rather than somewhere that will.

And here's the thing about caves, since nobody's told you: they fight differently. Tight rooms, narrow tunnels. On open ground you take them one at a time because they come to you one at a time. Step into the wrong corner down there and you'll have three on you at once.

I don't want a report of what you fought. I want what you NOTICED - water where there shouldn't be any, a draught, the shape of a room before you're standing in the middle of it.

That's the difference between surviving this valley and being remembered by it.
quests.accept_text: Nakhtar talks. I'd rather you see something with your own eyes and tell me what you found. The Den is close, shallow, forgiving - as caves go. And that's the other thing: caves aren't like open ground. Tight rooms, narrow tunnels - you step into the wrong corner and you'll have two or three of them on you at once instead of one. It's not a warning to scare you off. It's just how caves fight. Go in. Look around properly - not just at what's trying to kill you. Come back and tell me what you noticed.
quests.turn_in_text: You're still in one piece, and better - you came back describing a place, not just a fight. That instinct is worth more than any weapon I could hand you. Most people who wake up in this valley never learn to look past what's directly in front of them. You're already ahead of most.

quests.title: The Nest Guardian
quests.description:
The thing in the Den has stopped lurking and started patrolling. That makes it either a real problem or a very useful lesson and I see no reason it can't be both.

I'll not dress this up for you. It isn't the worst thing in this valley - it isn't close - but it is the first thing you'll meet that can actually kill you if you get sloppy.

Everything until now has punished carelessness with a scar. Boars, scorpids, a bad step in the dark. This one punishes it with your life.

I want you to feel that difference now. On my terms, in a fight I'm confident you can win, with me close enough to be useful - rather than discovering it in six months somewhere I am not.

It's a soft one, as these go. Don't get comfortable because I said soft.
quests.accept_text: It's a soft boss, as these things go in this valley. But it's still a boss, and you haven't fought one yet. Don't get comfortable just because I called it soft. Go find out what your hands do when the stakes are real.
quests.turn_in_text: You did it. However your hands are shaking right now, if they are - remember exactly how this felt. That was your first real fight in this world, and it will not be your last. The next one won't announce itself as a lesson the way this one did. Carry that with you.

quests.title: Fel Taint
quests.description:
Demons. In this valley.

I've stood this watch three seasons. Three. And in all that time I never saw so much as a whiff of fel energy anywhere near this ridge, and now there's a cave full of it up at the Burning Blade Coven.

That's not a complaint about my posting, though I've got several. It's that this valley is YOUNG. Nothing has had time to go wrong here yet. Whatever opened that door, it didn't open by itself and it didn't open here by accident.

I'm not asking you to solve it. I'm asking you to thin the familiars out and buy us breathing room while somebody with more rank than me works out what we're looking at.

And don't go past the familiars on your own. That part isn't advice.
quests.accept_text: Demons. In this valley, of all places. I've stood this watch three seasons and never seen one before last week - now there's a cave full of them. Whatever's in there isn't from around here either, kind of like you, maybe, though I doubt it's as friendly. Start with the familiars. Don't go deeper without backup.
quests.turn_in_text: Four down, and the cave's gone quiet - for now. Quiet isn't the same as safe, and I want you to remember that before you get comfortable. Whatever's still in there commanding them hasn't so much as flinched. That's the part that keeps me up at night, if orcs still dreamed the way you people do.

quests.title: Baneshadow
quests.description:
It's got a name now. We pulled it out of a familiar before the thing stopped answering questions altogether.

Yarrog Baneshadow. That's what's been giving the orders in that cave.

Here's how he fights, and I'd rather you heard it from me than found out in the dark: he summons. The longer the fight runs, the more of them are in the room with you, and if you let it turn into a long fight you will end up fighting the whole coven at once with your back to a wall.

The answer isn't clever. It's discipline. Ignore the noise, go for the head of the snake, finish it fast.

Kill him and whatever foothold the fel has carved here dies with him. I'd go myself if the valley could spare the watch. It can't. So it's you.
quests.accept_text: He summons more of them the longer the fight runs - don't let them stack up on you, or you'll be fighting the whole coven at once. Focus him, finish it fast. I'd go myself if the valley could spare the watch. It can't. So it's you.
quests.turn_in_text: Baneshadow is dead, and the valley is a little less wrong than it was this morning. I watched that fight end from the ridge - you didn't hesitate once. Whatever you were before you fell into this world, you fight like someone who's done this before, in some life or another. Maybe that's just how it works for people like you. Well fought, all the same. Truly.

quests.title: Sagewood Petals
quests.description:
You've got that look. The one they all have when they first wake up here, like the ground isn't quite convinced it's holding you.

It passes. Give it a week and stop thinking about it.

Marta. I've tended more disoriented strangers through this valley than I can count and I stopped asking where any of them came from a long time ago, which you may find restful.

What I need is practical. Sagewood petals, from the sprites in the grove, for a remedy I'm brewing - half the recruits come back off that ridge with scorpid venom in them and the other half will.

The sprites drop them when they're startled badly enough to run. It isn't dangerous work, it's patient work, and you look steady enough for both. Fresh as you can manage, they wilt fast.
quests.accept_text: You've got that look - the one they all have when they first wake up here, like the ground itself doesn't feel quite real yet. It passes, given time. In the meantime, the sagewood sprites drop petals when they're startled badly enough to run. Bring me five, fresh as you can manage - they wilt fast.
quests.turn_in_text: Still fragrant - you were careful with these, good. Most recruits crush half of what they bring me without noticing. You'll do fine here, better than fine maybe, if you keep paying that kind of attention to the small things. It's usually the small things that keep people alive out here.

quests.title: Hounds of the Coven
quests.description:
You'll meet the hounds before the familiars, most likely.

The demons brought their own dogs with them - whelps, and the smaller pups running with them. Quick, vicious, and bred for precisely one thing, which they do well.

I don't care which of the two you put down. A dead hound is a dead hound, whelp or pup, and anybody who tells you different is making conversation.

Do it while you're in there for the rest of it. No sense making two trips into a cave full of demons for the sake of tidiness.
quests.accept_text: You'll see the hounds before you see the familiars, most likely - whelps and pups both, running in packs. Doesn't matter which you kill. Six dead hounds is six dead hounds, whichever kind they are.
quests.turn_in_text: Good. Fewer teeth in that cave now. Between you and whoever else the valley sends in, maybe we actually clear it out before something worse decides to move in behind the demons.

quests.title: Beyond the Valley
quests.description:
Come here. Sit down - no, properly sit, this is the last time I'll get to say any of this.

This valley hasn't got much left to teach you. The boars, the scorpids, the coven's demons - you've handled everything this place can throw at a green recruit, and standing here collecting more of the same would only make you confident about the wrong things.

Razor Hill sits at the heart of Durotar. It's a real town, with real orcs making real lives in it, and it's time you saw one.

Follow the road east and keep it under your feet the whole way. Durotar doesn't forgive wandering off the road - not yet, not for someone still as green as you are underneath everything you've survived here.

Find Weapons Trainer Grokk. Tell him I sent you, though I expect he'll know the moment he sees how you carry yourself.
quests.accept_text: Follow the road east out of the valley and keep it under your feet the whole way - Durotar doesn't forgive wandering off it, not yet, not for someone as green as you still are underneath everything you've survived here. Razor Hill sits at the heart of it. Find Grokk. Tell him Nakhtar sent you, though I suspect he'll know the second he sees you carry yourself.
quests.turn_in_text:
[Grokk looks you over without hurrying about it.]

Nakhtar. He didn't need to send word - you've got the valley all over you. Everyone who comes up that road does.

Right. Whatever you learned down there was about staying alive. Here you'll learn what to do with the time that buys you.

quests.title: Wanted: Old Tusk
quests.description:
Six seasons I've watched this ridge and I know every boar on it by its tracks.

There's one set I don't like. Boar the size of a cart, tusks worn yellow, and it walks straight through the training dummies on Sagebrush Flat - not round them, THROUGH them, like the dummies have said something.

The recruits call it Old Tusk, which is the sort of name you give a thing when you've decided it's funny rather than dangerous.

I call it a matter of time before somebody's mother gets bad news.

Thin the boars on the flat, and when the old one shows himself, put him down. He's the one that doesn't run. Don't fight him on open ground with your back to a hill - use the dummies. He hates the dummies.
quests.accept_text: West of camp, on the flat. You'll know him when you see him - he's the one that doesn't run. Don't fight him on open ground with your back to a hill. Use the dummies. He hates the dummies.
quests.turn_in_text: Tusk's down? Good. Good. That's a lot of years of that animal off the ridge in one afternoon. Take these - the old boar's had them coming since before you woke up.

quests.title: Carrion Circle
quests.description:
Don't tell Nakhtar I'm giving out work. He's got views about what a man on his back should be doing with his day.

Torgak. I can't walk the ridge yet and the carrion birds have noticed.

They've started circling the camp in the afternoons. Patient, the way a tax collector is patient. And the jackals that follow them have been creeping in closer to the fire each night, because jackals only get brave when there's something circling.

It's nothing personal.

[A pause.]

They think I'm already dead. I would very much like to change their minds, and I would like it done where they can see it happening.

Birds first. The jackals lose their nerve on their own after that.
quests.accept_text: They think I'm already dead. I'd like to change their minds. Vultures first - the jackals only get brave when there's something circling. Don't tell Nakhtar I'm giving out quests.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet sky. You have no idea how nice that is. Take something - Nakhtar says I'm not allowed to hand out coin, but nobody said anything about gear I can't wear anymore.

quests.title: Troubled Waters
quests.description:
The spring at the lake south of camp has fed this valley since before the Horde had a name for itself.

I can't get a clean batch out of it.

The marsh skimmers are skating the shallows in numbers I've not seen in my lifetime here, and the toads have gone bold - and a bold toad is a small thing that tells you something larger is going on, which I'd rather not think about before I've had a brew that works.

I'm not asking for a massacre. I want enough dead things that the water runs clear.

Go south. Mind the mud, it's deeper than it looks. Skimmers or toads, I don't care which you reach first - I just want the shallows still for an hour.
quests.accept_text: Go south to the lake. Mind the mud, it's deeper than it looks. Skimmers and toads - I don't care which you reach first, I just want the shallows still for an hour.
quests.turn_in_text: Clear water, at last. Smell that? That's a remedy that works. And look at you - hardly wet. You're learning the trick of it faster than most.

quests.title: The Spring's Warden
quests.description:
The skimmers were the symptom. I thought they might be.

Something's taken up residence at Trailwater Spring. A toad bigger than a boar - the recruits have started calling it Old Gulpjaw, in the tone people use for weather they can't do anything about.

It's been eating whatever drifts in. Now it's eating whatever walks in, and the difference between those two sentences is the reason I'm asking.

I need my spring back.

He sits at the bottom of the shallows and waits. Don't wade in after him - everything slow is worse in water than out of it. Pull him onto the bank and fight him there.

Bring a friend if you can find one. Bring a plan if you can't.
quests.accept_text: He sits at the bottom of the shallows and waits. Don't wade in. Pull him out onto the bank - everything slow is worse in water than out of it.
quests.turn_in_text: Gulpjaw, gone. The water's already settling. You've done this valley more good than you know - and I'll keep telling people so, whether you like it or not.

quests.title: Heartwood and Thorn
quests.description:
The petals did their job and the recruits are keeping their feet. Now I want the thing that makes the petals worth gathering in the first place.

Heartwood, out of the old sagewood in the grove east of camp.

There's a difficulty. The saplings in there have started walking - thornroots, quick and mean and entirely new this season. And something older has begun moving among them.

Bramblethorn has been in that grove longer than this valley has had a name. Longer than the Horde, if you believe my grandmother, and I generally did.

I'm not asking you to fell it. I want that said plainly, because somebody will tell you later that I did.

I'm asking that it stop.
quests.accept_text: It's the grove's own heart gone sour. Saplings first - they'll tell you where the old one is. Fire works, if you have it. It also makes the grove very angry, so do it quickly.
quests.turn_in_text: The grove's quiet again. Listen to it. That is what a valley sounds like when it isn't being watched. Take something. You've earned more than I'll ever be able to give.

quests.title: The Brood Below
quests.description:
You came back from the Den's mouth with your eyes working. Good. Now the deeper chambers.

That cave is a brood. That's what it's FOR - it isn't a lair that happens to have eggs in it, it's a nursery with guards, and the guards are only ever as dangerous as the numbers standing behind them.

Skitterers and webspinners in the halls. Egg tenders in the nursery itself.

Thin them out, and do it in that order, so that whoever eventually goes for the guardian isn't fighting it in a room full of its children.

That's not squeamishness. A fight in a nursery is a fight where every single thing in the room has a reason to be reckless.
quests.accept_text: Caves lie. They tell you the next room is safe because it's quiet. Then you step in and find out why it was quiet. Clear the halls, then the nursery. One room at a time.
quests.turn_in_text: You walk different than you did. Good. Fewer of them behind you means fewer in front. The guardian is next, and it's the last thing in that cave that matters.

quests.title: Windrift Omens
quests.description:
I read weather the way other orcs read faces, and the weather in the Windrift Dunes is saying something I don't care for.

Dust devils walking the road. Not drifting across it - WALKING it, along its length, with the sort of consistency that stops being weather somewhere around the third day.

And the sandpincers keep pushing up out of ground where there was nothing before. I've dug. There's no burrow under them. They are arriving rather than emerging.

I want the dunes quiet before whatever is stirring them finishes waking up and takes an interest in which direction the camp is.

Go south-east. Don't stand still on open sand.
quests.accept_text: Southeast, down the road to the dunes. Don't chase the dust. Let it come to you. Sandpincers hide under the surface - if the sand moves, move first.
quests.turn_in_text: Quieter already. I can hear the road again. There's one more place that's wrong, and it's the worst one. We'll talk about it.

quests.title: The Cinderjaw Problem
quests.description:
[Kuraw takes a while to start.]

Far to the south-west the ground itself is burnt. We call it the Cinderjaw Wastes and no one goes there, and for most of my life that was a sensible arrangement that required no thought.

Ember wisps drift across it like loose sparks. Ashback basilisks sleep on the warm stone. And there is something out there the scouts have named Smolderhide, which walks at night with fire on its back.

The wastes are creeping toward the lake. Slowly. But I've watched the edge for eleven years and I know where it used to be.

This is the hardest thing I have ever asked a recruit to do. I want you to understand that I know it, and that I'm asking anyway, and that if you'd rather not I will think no less of you and will not raise it again.
quests.accept_text: Go south, past the lake, and keep the road under your feet until it stops being a road. Don't fight on the black stone. It holds heat. Smolderhide will find you - it always finds you. Be ready when it does.
quests.turn_in_text: Smolderhide, dead. Then the valley's dangerous things are done, or as done as they get. You have the look of someone who survived a lot. That's the only graduation I recognize.

quests.title: Grosk's Trophy
quests.description:
Right - you're the one everyone's talking about. Good. Listen.

A real orc doesn't just leave this valley. He leaves it with a trophy. That's the whole of my thinking and I've been working on it for a while.

I've picked Sandfang. The pale one, all scars, out in the Windrift Dunes - he's outrun every hunter in this valley including two who were genuinely good.

[A pause.]

I haven't worked out how yet. That's the part where you come in and I'd be grateful if you didn't make a thing of it.

Thin the pack, find the old one, bring me proof.

My mother has views about this entire idea. She may well be right. We're doing it anyway.
quests.accept_text: It's a white one. Scar over the left eye. Quick as anything, but it's old - old things get careless. I'd do it myself except... my mother. You understand.
quests.turn_in_text: You actually did it! She's going to be so angry. I'm going to tell everyone you did it, I swear - I'll say it was both of us. Here, take something. For the trouble.

quests.title: Fizzcrank's Shiny Problem
quests.description:
You! Yes, you, the one who isn't on fire. Perfect.

Fizzcrank Sprocketspin. The crystals lining that Coven give off a heat that I find personally offensive, and I want you to understand I mean that technically rather than emotionally.

It should not be possible for a thing to be warm AND wrong at the same time. Warm is a measurement. Wrong is a judgement. Those are different departments and something in that cave has them filed together.

Get me shards. Small ones - pocket-sized, the kind the acolytes keep on their belts, not the big ones in the walls because I've seen what happened to the last fellow.

I'm fairly sure they're not dangerous.

I'm also fairly sure that one was on fire a moment ago. Both can be true.
quests.accept_text: The acolytes keep them on their belts. Don't touch them with bare hands. Use tongs. Or a stick. Or a different hand. I'll be here, doing my own science.
quests.turn_in_text: Oh, that's wonderful. That's - oh no. Okay, it's fine, nothing to see. Take whatever you want from the bench - I'm going to be busy.

quests.title: Silk for Rhaka
quests.description:
My son went up the ridge last week to prove himself.

He came back. I'd like to keep that arrangement going, and in my experience the surest way is a good cloak.

Not a ratty hide thing off a vendor's cart. Silk - proper silk, strong enough to turn a scorpid sting, the sort the webspinners make in the halls of the Den.

I have the loom. I've had the loom since my mother's day and I know exactly what I'd do with the spools.

I do not have the nerve to go into that cave, and I'd rather say so to your face than invent a reason. I've stood at the mouth of it twice.

Bring me the silk and he'll have the cloak before the next climb.
quests.accept_text: Spools, from the webspinners. They keep them at their backs. Don't take the loose thread - it's sticky. The spools are what you want. Be careful. Please.
quests.turn_in_text: This is good silk. Strong. Feel that? That'll turn a stinger. Here - I made extra. It's the least I can do for the one who made me less afraid.

quests.title: Mother of the Nest
quests.description:
The scorpids you've been killing have a mother. I thought you should know that from me rather than from her.

Broodmother Sarrix has held the north-eastern nest longer than the Horde has held this valley. She's the reason the workers keep coming and she'll be the reason they keep coming after you've thinned them twice more.

I am not asking you to fight her.

I'm asking you to fight everything around her first - the venomtails, the ones that will be at her side when it matters - and then to stand at the edge of that nest and decide honestly whether you're ready.

[He looks at you.]

I suspect you'll go anyway. I'd rather you went having been asked to think about it.
quests.accept_text: Northeast. Past the camp road, where the sand turns dark. She rarely leaves the nest and never leaves it unguarded. Be sure of your health before you commit to the fight. It's long, and it's patient.
quests.turn_in_text: Sarrix is dead. The nest will keep moving without her for a season and then settle. You did something this valley has needed for a long time. I won't forget it.

quests.title: Disrupting the Ritual
quests.description:
The familiars were bait. I want to be plain about that, because I sent you at them and I'd rather own it.

Deeper in the Coven they've been drawing a circle. A real one, in a hall I've only ever seen from the mouth of the passage, and there is a summoning going into it.

Initiates hold the approaches and the ritual guards stand between them and anybody with a sword and an opinion.

Break it up before it finishes.

Because if that circle closes there won't be a Baneshadow to go and fight afterwards. There'll be whatever Baneshadow has spent all this effort trying to get hold of, and I don't have a plan for that and neither does anybody above me.
quests.accept_text: Initiates in the outer halls. Ritual guards in the hall with the circle. Kill the guards first if you can - they're the ones who'll finish it. I'll hold the road behind you.
quests.turn_in_text: The circle's broken. The air smells normal again, and I didn't know I'd been smelling it. There's only one left to finish. Take this and go.
